title: Working at Redwood — roles, careers, benefits, hiring & internal tools
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview

This page is the single-source reference for what it means to work at Redwood: our role families and career ladders, core benefits and perks, a high-level view of the hiring and onboarding process, and the internal tools new hires should know. It is intended for all employees and hiring managers. For role-specific contribution guides, see the linked role ladder pages in the Careers section.

1) Working at Redwood — guiding principles

- Developer-first product focus: we prioritize engineering excellence, clear ownership, and shipping reliable inference for customers.
- Growth-minded culture: consistent feedback, transparent ladders, and meaningful career development.
- Remote-first with HQ hubs: we are distributed across NA, EU and growing in APAC; teams coordinate asynchronously with regular alignment rituals.
- Production-first safety: reliability, security, and data protection are part of shipping features.

2) Role families and career ladders (summary)

We maintain explicit ladders for each role family. Leveling is handled by People Ops together with hiring managers; calibration cycles run quarterly. Typical families and canonical titles:

- Engineering: Software Engineer I/II/Senior/Staff/Principal/Distinguished (IC1–IC6)
- Engineering Management: Eng Manager / Senior EM / Director / Senior Director
- Product: Associate Product Manager / Product Manager / Senior PM / Principal PM
- Applied ML & Research: Applied ML Engineer / Research Scientist / Senior / Principal
- SRE & Infra: SRE / Senior SRE / Staff SRE
- Design, Data, Customer Success, Sales, Finance, Legal, People Ops (respective ladders)

Career ladder expectations (high level)

| Level | Typical title examples | Typical tenure | Core expectations |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| IC2 | Software Engineer II | 1–3 years | Owns medium-scope projects, writes reliable code, participates in design reviews |
| IC3 | Senior Engineer | 3–6 years | Leads large features, mentors others, influences architecture and quality |
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | 5+ years | Shapes cross-team initiatives, technical roadmap, measurable impact on cost/latency |
| IC5 | Principal Engineer | 8+ years | Company-level technical leadership, long-term platform strategy |

Promotion process (summary)

1. Candidate (or manager) opens a promotion packet in People Ops (template in Careers folder).
2. Manager prepares evidence: project summaries, impact metrics (latency/cost/uptime improvements), peer reviews, and goal alignment.
3. Promotion review meeting with calibration panel (manager, peer director, People Ops).
4. Decision recorded in HR system; feedback and next steps shared with the candidate.

3) Benefits & perks (current as of last_updated date above)

Health & financial
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contributions (US plans include HMO and PPO options).
- 401(k) with employer match up to 4% after 6 months.
- Equity grants: new hires receive an initial RSU grant with standard 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff (role-level dependent).

Time off & leaves
- Flexible paid time off (PTO) with recommended minimum of 15 days per year for full-time employees; managers approve time off in accordance with team coverage.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks fully paid primary leave, 6 weeks secondary leave; additional unpaid leave subject to local law.
- Company holidays: 10 observed days plus 1 floating day and regional closures.

Family & wellness
- $1,000 annual wellness stipend for therapy, fitness, or ergonomic equipment.
- Dependent care FSAs where available.

Learning & remote work allowances
- $1,200 annual learning stipend (courses, conferences, certifications).
- Home office stipend on hire ($500) and reimbursement for desk/chair upgrades on request.

Perks & additional programs
- Commuter/transportation benefits where applicable.
- Regular internal tech talks, cross-functional offsites, and a mentorship program (People Ops-run).

Note: Specific plan details and eligibility vary by country and employment type. Refer to Benefits Portal (HR system link) for plan PDFs and carrier contacts.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- PLG-led growth requires high engineering velocity and quality; we hire for product-obsessed, collaborative engineers and cross-functional partners.
- Diversity and inclusive hiring are required: all roles use structured interviews and standardized scorecards.

Typical interview process (engineering example)
1. Recruiter screen (30m) — role fit, background, salary range, relocation/work authorization if relevant.
2. Technical screen (45–60m) — coding, system design primer for senior roles.
3. Onsite/loop (4–5 interviews, 3 hours) — includes coding, system design, behavioral, and team-collaboration interviews.
4. Hiring packet & calibration — interviewers submit scorecards into the hiring ATS; hiring manager compiles a packet for the hiring committee.
5. Offer & negotiation — People Ops/Recruiter extend offer, coordinate compensation and start date.

Interview scorecard guidance
- Use the standard scorecard template (link in Careers folder). Score cards evaluate: problem solving, technical craft, systems thinking, collaboration, ownership, and alignment with company values.

Onboarding checklist (first 30 days)
- Day 0 (pre-start): hardware shipped, access to SSO and email, welcome packet sent. Owner: People Ops.
- Day 1: Orientation (company overview, policies), team intro, first-week schedule. Owner: People Ops + Hiring Manager.
- Week 1: Setup dev environment (GitHub, CI creds, local run instructions), join team standups, first small ticket assigned. Owner: Hiring Manager + Buddy.
- Week 2–4: Deep dives with product/infra docs, shadowing sessions, deliver first scoped bug/feature. Owner: Manager + Mentor.
- 30-day check-in: manager and People Ops run a progress review and adjust goals.

New hire buddy program
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy for the first 90 days (not the direct manager). Buddies help with day-to-day questions, culture, and tooling.

Hiring manager responsibilities (quick reference)
- Prepare onboarding plan before start date.
- Ensure hardware and access are provisioned by Day 0.
- Schedule 1:1s weekly for first 90 days and run a 30/60/90 plan.

5) Internal tools guide (quickstart & ownership)

Central tools and access flow
- Identity: Okta SSO. Owner: Security & IT. New hires receive SSO invite from People Ops.
- Messaging: Slack (org-wide channels and private team channels). Owner: Eng Dev.
- Code: GitHub (organization access, team repo permissions). Owner: Eng Platform.
- Issue tracking: Linear for product & engineering boards. Owner: Product Ops.
- CI/CD: Buildkite (pipeline templates under infra repo). Owner: Eng Infra.
- Cloud accounts: GCP primary, AWS for legacy workloads. Access granted via Okta groups and IAM roles. Owner: Cloud Platform.
- Secrets & keys: HashiCorp Vault for runtime secrets; SSM Parameter Store for managed infra keys. Owner: Security/Cloud Platform.
- Documentation: Confluence (this space) for policies, Notion for product PRDs. Owner: Eng Dev + Product.
- Monitoring & Alerts: Datadog dashboards for latency/cost dashboards; alerting rules in PagerDuty. Owner: SRE.

First-week technical setup checklist
1. Complete Okta activation and MFA.
2. Join Redwood Slack and relevant channels (#engineering, #announcements, team channels).
3. Accept GitHub invite(s) and set up SSH keys.
4. Clone the repo and run the local dev quickstart: repo root README > scripts/setup-local.sh.
5. Request access to cloud projects with the cloud-access request form (link).
6. Verify Datadog access for observability dashboards.
7. Confirm Buildkite and CI token access by running the sample pipeline (instructions in infra/ci-cd README).

Self-service access requests
- Use the Access Portal (internal link) to request additional permissions; approvals route to service owners and are logged in the change control system.

Tooling runbook snippets
- GitHub branch policy: all PRs require at least one code-owner approval and a green CI run. For release branches, require 2 approvals.
- Deploy process: create PR to infra/deploy-config, include release notes, and add on-call SRE to reviewers. For Dedicated/private deployments, also include security sign-off.

6) People Ops contacts, escalation, and feedback loops

- People Ops leads: Priya Patel (Head of People Ops) — priya@redwood.example.com; Iris Nguyen (Recruiting Lead) — iris@redwood.example.com.
- For leveling questions or disputes, open a ticket in People Ops (Leveling review queue).
- To request accommodations or discuss parental leave, contact benefits@redwood.example.com.
